title: Canadian–American Reciprocity Treaty
text: The Canadian–American Reciprocity Treaty of 1854, also known as the Elgin-Marcy Treaty after its key negotiators, James Bruce, 8th Earl of Elgin and William L. Marcy, was a treaty between the United Kingdom and the United States that applied to British North America, including the Province of Canada, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland Colony. The treaty covered raw materials; in effect from 1854 to 1866, it represented a move toward free trade and was opposed by protectionist elements in the United States.
